title: Chronic actinic dermatitis
summary: A persistent, severe, eczematous photodermatosis, usually in older men, affecting the face, neck and backs of the hands with sharp cut-offs at clothing. Often linked to contact allergy (Compositae, fragrance) and needs specialist phototesting.

glance.think: Thickened, itchy eczema on the face, scalp, neck and backs of hands in an older man, sparing the upper eyelids, behind the ears and under the chin.
glance.engine: Extreme sensitivity to UVB, UVA and sometimes visible light, behaving like contact allergy to an endogenous light-altered antigen; contact allergy is common alongside.
glance.backbone: Strict photoprotection (including visible light), emollients, potent topical steroid or tacrolimus; refer for phototesting and patch testing; specialist immunosuppression.
glance.never_miss: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and drug photosensitivity as mimics; erythroderma.

what: A **chronic, persistent, often severe eczema of sun-exposed skin** caused by abnormal sensitivity to UVB, often UVA and sometimes visible light. Typically affects **older men (60+), usually fair-skinned**, in the UK; also seen in younger people with darker skin types and in people with longstanding atopic eczema. Older synonyms: persistent light reaction, photosensitive eczema, actinic reticuloid (severe pseudolymphomatous end of the spectrum).
cause: Thought to be a **delayed-type hypersensitivity (allergic contact-type) reaction to an endogenous skin antigen photo-modified by UV** — i.e. "photo-allergy to one's own skin". Strong links with **contact allergy**: up to ~3/4 have positive patch tests, especially to **Compositae (sesquiterpene lactones — chrysanthemums, daisies, dandelions)**, fragrance, colophony, rubber chemicals and **sunscreen filters**. May follow a photoallergic drug reaction (persistent light reaction) or airborne contact dermatitis. Cumulative sun damage and outdoor work/gardening/hobbies in older men are risk factors. Some drugs (thiazides, certain antibiotics) can aggravate it.

list: **Itchy, red, thickened, lichenified eczematous plaques** on face (forehead, cheeks, nose), scalp in bald men, ears, **back and sides of neck, V of chest, dorsal hands/forearms**.
**Sharp cut-off** at collar and wrist/cuff; **sparing** of upper eyelids, skin creases, behind/under ears, under chin, finger webs (DermNet gallery).
Can extend to covered sites and progress to **erythroderma** in severe cases.
Present year-round but worse in summer; patients may say even indoor light/fluorescent light triggers flares.
Darker skin: hyperpigmentation and lichenification more than redness.
Severe: infiltrated papules/plaques with atypical lymphocytes (actinic reticuloid) — mimics cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (Sézary syndrome).
**Monochromator phototesting** (photobiology unit): reduced minimal erythema dose to UVB ± UVA ± visible — confirms diagnosis and guides photoprotection.
**Patch testing and photopatch testing** (Compositae mix, fragrance, sunscreen agents, plant extracts).
Biopsy: chronic spongiotic dermatitis ± atypical lymphoid infiltrate; exclude lymphoma (Sézary cells, T-cell receptor gene studies if erythrodermic).
Bloods: ANA/ENA (exclude lupus), porphyrins; HIV in younger patients with new severe photosensitivity.

head: Look-alike
Distinguishing clues
rows: Involves **shaded** sites too (upper eyelids, under chin, behind ears); patch tests; may coexist with CAD
Temporal link to drug; resolves after stopping (persistent light reaction = CAD-like evolution)
Younger, intermittent, clears within weeks, not lichenified
Central face, papulopustules, telangiectasia, flushing; no eczema

management: **Refer to dermatology** (phototesting/patch testing are specialist). While waiting and long-term:

list: **Rigorous photoprotection** (UVB, UVA ± visible): broad-spectrum SPF 50+ high UVA, **fragrance-free**, ideally **mineral/tinted** if visible-light sensitive or sunscreen-allergic; wide-brimmed hats, long sleeves, gloves, UV-protective window film; avoid sun 10:00–16:00.
**Allergen avoidance** per patch tests (e.g. Compositae plants in garden, fragrance).

**Topical corticosteroids** — potent to body/hands; moderate short courses to face; **topical calcineurin inhibitors** (tacrolimus 0.1%/pimecrolimus — off-label for CAD, specialist-guided) as steroid-sparing on the face. Counsel: TCIs can cause transient burning; strict sun protection while using them.
Specialist systemic: **azathioprine**, ciclosporin, mycophenolate, methotrexate, dupilumab (case reports); low-dose PUVA/narrowband UVB under steroid cover (hardening) in selected patients.
**Vitamin D supplementation** (10 micrograms daily, or check levels) because of strict sun avoidance.

management: Suspected CAD → routine dermatology (photobiology). **Urgent** if erythrodermic, systemically unwell, lymphadenopathy or atypical infiltrated plaques (exclude lymphoma).
red_flags: Erythroderma or rapidly spreading eczema: same-day dermatology.
Persistent photosensitive eczema in an older adult: refer for **phototesting and patch testing**.
pearls: "Eczema in an older man that is worst on the face, neck and backs of hands — and spares behind the ears" = think CAD.
Patients may be sensitised to their **own sunscreen** — choose fragrance-free, minimal-filter or physical products and ask about reactions.
Gardening is a double hit (UV + Compositae): gloves, long sleeves, avoid chrysanthemums/daisies if allergic.
Severe disease can be life-limiting (house-bound): signpost BAD leaflet and support; consider mental health.
Many improve over years with strict avoidance.
